item.title: Respond to an audience question
item.summary: A speaker corrects a misleading interpretation of an attendance figure.
item.transcript_text:
Host: You said attendance rose by twenty per cent after the museum introduced evening hours. Does that mean the late opening attracted a new audience?
Researcher: It shows we counted more entries per week, including repeat visits. We didn't ask when each person first started visiting.
Host: So the extra time might simply have made return visits easier?
Researcher: Exactly. It's a possibility, not a verdict. A short exit question about first-time visits would help, as long as we asked it at both daytime and evening sessions.
Host: That seems less dramatic than the press headline.
Researcher: It is also a result we can actually check.

questions.prompt: What does the twenty per cent refer to?
options: People who answered the exit survey
questions.explanation: An entry is a visit. The count includes repeat visits.

questions.prompt: What is the researcher's view of the suggested explanation?
options: It is plausible but still untested
It has been ruled out by the data
It is the only possible explanation
It must be accepted because the headline says so
questions.explanation: The researcher explicitly calls it a possibility rather than a conclusion.

questions.prompt: Why ask at both kinds of session?
options: To avoid having to count return visits
To compare whether the visitor mix differs by time
To guarantee that the museum attracts a new audience
questions.explanation: Collecting the same first-visit information at different times makes that comparison possible.

children.segment_text: at both daytime and evening sessions
